description: The mouse aims with raw input only: a thread with a message-only window registered for the mouse (RIDEV_INPUTSINK) adds every relative report, in device counts, to 64-bit counters; IN_MouseMove hands CL_MouseEvent exactly those counts each frame instead of the cursor's movement. No Windows pointer speed or acceleration, no per-frame clamp, no other mouse mode; absolute reports (tablets, remote desktop) are ignored; movement made in the background and on the frame focus returns is dropped. The cursor is still read for the menus and kept in the window. Fixes B0010, B0011.

description: Aim in MW2019 units: one count turns the view by m_sens * 0.0066 degrees (m_sens default 1.5, archived), at any field of view, hip fire and ADS alike: no cgameFOVSensitivityScale, cl_mouseAccel, m_filter, m_yaw or m_pitch. functions: iw6mp64_MSStore_ship 14062F420 R_CreateDevice; 140631A80 R_RecoverLostDevice (with the R_ResetDevice it inlines); 140675C50 RB_SwapBuffers; import CreateDXGIFactory (enhanced/gfx_d3d/r_init.cpp)
description: Flip-model presentation: the swap chain is DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_FLIP_DISCARD with two buffers (Windows can then hand the game's buffers straight to the display: independent flip, in fullscreen and in a borderless window covering the monitor), from a DXGI 1.1 factory (CreateDXGIFactory1). Tearing is allowed when IDXGIFactory5 reports support, and a windowed present with r_vsync 0 tears (uncapped or VRR). The device queues at most one frame (IDXGIDevice1::SetMaximumFrameLatency(1)). Flip model unbinds the back buffer at Present, so the render targets bound before it are bound again after it. A lost device's new swap chain is made the same way, after ClearState and Flush (one flip-model swap chain per window). A system that refuses a flip-model swap chain gets the original one. The frame-latency waitable object is P0004.

functions: iw6mp64_MSStore_ship 1406327D0 R_SyncGpu; 14062F420 R_CreateDevice, 140631A80 R_RecoverLostDevice and 140675C50 RB_SwapBuffers as in P0003; new: R_AcquireFrameLatencyWaitable, R_WaitForFrameLatency (enhanced/gfx_d3d/r_init.cpp)
description: Frame-latency wait: the flip-model swap chain is created with DXGI_SWAP_CHAIN_FLAG_FRAME_LATENCY_WAITABLE_OBJECT, IDXGISwapChain2::SetMaximumFrameLatency(1), and R_SyncGpu, right after the lost-device check and its first clock read (so the wait counts against com_maxfps), waits on the waitable object once for each present the render thread made since the last wait. The wait for present p returns once present p-1 is on screen: one frame stays queued while the next frame's mouse is read (IN_Frame runs right after R_SyncGpu in every client state). Pairing by counted presents means frames that weren't presented are never waited for. Each wait times out after two refresh periods (50 ms to 1 s) and is alertable. A timed-out wait, or a present the window procedure made (fullscreen switch), makes the next frame take every pending signal instead of counting. A lost device's new swap chain gets a new object and the counts start again. Falls back to no wait without IDXGISwapChain2 (flip model without the flag, then the original swap chain, when the system refuses it). Otherwise R_SyncGpu is the original, compared call for call with the Store build. Not yet: keys and mouse buttons are still read at the top of Com_Frame, before the wait (docs/frame.md section 5).
